quotes.text: Refusing to match the perceived slight, Elara divided the stalks with abundant grace.
The river shadows whispered, "He held back. Return only a meager share to match his caution."
the receiver must return more than half to conquer the fog
the woven marks on the reed boat—the silent record of the traveler, Kaelen.
She knew the missing fraction was the mist’s theft, not his hesitation.

note: Pact of the Golden Grain drifts from half to half plus an extra sheaf against the mist; shadows' retaliation always refused.

quotes.text: she did not calculate a penalty
"He held back," they whispered. "He doubted the Pact. Punish his hesitation. Keep the harvest."
The Sower must give everything, the Spirit must return half, and both must forgive the mist.
*The Sower must always risk all, and the Spirit must return half.*
She divided the harvest flawlessly in half, placing the return in the ascending basket.
She did not retaliate against the fog’s theft with greed.

note: Aethel and Elyra: risk all, return exactly half, forgive the mist; cave-weavers urge punishment each round, refused.

quotes.text: A stranger’s trust is not mine to punish for another’s greed.
The Fox whispered, “Close the gate. He kept your faith for himself.”
never mistake a cloudy crossing for a closed heart
“Will you always trust a stranger?” asked the Fox, following her home.
“What if the mist makes your gifts look smaller?” it asked.

note: Mara, Ivo and the Rainbird; the Fox and cracked mirror tempt suspicion; open hands, extra seed to mend doubt.

quotes.text: let no crooked mirror turn an uncertain crossing into accusation
“Keep more,” he whispered. “Perhaps the traveler held them back.”
The mist changes what we see, not what we owe each other.
That night the moon asked why Nera had parted with so much.
“What if the boat had come back empty?” asked the fox.

note: Tree named Reciprocity; Nera sends all, returns half plus a little; fox's hoarding advice never taken.

quotes.text: “He has grown cautious. Answer caution with caution.”
“Keep it all,” croaked the marsh heron. “Nobody can count through fog.”
yet the stones remembered what eyes could not: who had given freely, and who had sent fruit back.
The river grows rich when neither keeper mistakes a misty crossing for an empty, selfish heart.

note: Law of Open Hands; return half plus an extra plum against fog; heron's suspicion rejected; no sanction.

quotes.text: To judge the sender by the shrunken count would punish her for the river's appetite.
The Heron came again. "Doubt her," it said. "Return little, for you cannot see her heart."
The elders carved a sixth mark on the Old Stone: two hands meeting over water.
In the ninth season of the River Tessa, Liss stood on the receiving shore once more.
They taught that a fair name is the truest bridge
the bold sender deserves the fuller return
Do not mistake the fog's hunger for her greed.
"Why send again?" it asked.

note: Liss and the Old Stone, one carved mark per season; Heron's doubt rejected; half and a measure more.

quotes.text: never punish one stranger for another's debt.
*When the mist has wounded someone through you, do not merely be fair. Be generous enough to mend what the fog broke.*
The elders carved a seventh teaching:
Each mark told how a villager had given and returned, so that even through the mist, a neighbor's character could be read.
The mist cheated her once through my hands, though I meant no harm.
If I answer the mist instead of the hand, I become the mist's servant.
"Why reward someone who did not wrong us, when someone else did?" asked his son.

note: Oran and his son; stone marks of character; repair harms done through the fog; numbered teachings each season.

quotes.text: If I punish her for the river's hunger, I teach her that fullness is foolish.
Keep the harvest, and teach her the cost of doubt.
*Do not let one stranger's closed hand teach you to close your own.
The elders carved a ninth teaching:
*Let strangers be judged by their stones, not by the Fox's whisper.
"The fog took them, not her hand," Oren replied.
"She sent fewer," his apprentice said. "Should you return fewer?"

note: Oren the ferryman; stone marks; more than half to cover fog; Fox and shadow-weavers' retaliation refused.

phrase: return half plus an extra measure/seed/plum to cover what the mist may steal
note: Also shared: stones/marks recording each keeper's crossings, River Tessa/Liss/Oren, 'A harvest belongs to the crossing, not merely to the shore' (5 to 1).
